Good value for money local Vietnamese in a shopping mall
Dec 2019 • Family
Good sampling of local Vietnamese cuisine in the convenience of a Hanoi shopping mall next to Lotte hotel. What caught our eye was the charming restaurant decor in a traditional Vietnamese sort of way. Do Take note that not all staff are English speaking as we discovered and may not understand your requests 😩

We tried a variety of local cuisine including beef pho, fish soup, noodles with beef and crab, local vegetables and mango salad. The pho was subjective as we had tasted various versions previously in Ho Chi Minh City but it was still good value for money and tasted good. While the fish soup was sumptuous, the fish head tasted gamely even though it was deep fried. We suspected that it could be a farm reared fish. The mango salad was refreshingly good and didn’t disappoint. Overall, good value for money on the basis of convenience and schedule as most Restsurants are closed after 2pm

A great variety of local cuisine
Jun 2019 • Friends
Most Vietnamese street foods are found in locations that serve only one of the huge variety of local options. This is a good place to go if you want to try a wide variety. The food safety concerns that some might have in general are not an issue. The is a clean and safe restaurant to order whatever you want and enjoy it - to include salads. That said, you can expect to pay higher prices for street food than you would on the street. The dishes here are 2-3 times higher than on the street. But, they are all located in the same place and are clean and safe for everyone to enjoy.

37th Street in Saigon Center - good representation of Vietnamese foods
Oct 2017 • Family
Once you step into 37th Street, it's like traveling back in time and you'll know exactly what kinds of food you'll be expecting - traditional Vietnamese street foods. Simply love that they paid attention to details in terms of decorating the stores, the intentionally lowered wooden tables and benches, the stone pavement, the dessert cart and even the cutlery ooze old-school Vietnamese charm. What's even better, for such a well-crafted experience, you only need to pay less than usd5 for a satisfying meal here, or maybe even less. 

It's a must-go if you want to try a wide variety of Vietnamese foods in a fun-looking environment, comfortable with air-conditioning, and presumably much cleaner and safer to eat at than roadside stores.
